newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Heavy shelling batters Somali capital.
newsitem.headline: Heavy shelling batters Somali capital.

text.p: Shelling battered parts of the Somali capital Mogadishu on Wednesday and aid workers said they feared more than 300 people had been killed in six days of battles.
Witnesses said warring factions in the south of the city exchanged fierce artillery and mortar fire in the afternoon after a morning of sporadic shooting on frontlines around Medina district
They said forces under Moslem fundamentalist leader Musa Sudi Yalahow in Medina, which is virtually besieged, traded fire with gunners of south Mogadishu faction chief Hussein Aideed.
Militiamen loyal to north Mogadishu alliance chief Ali Mahdi Mohamed on Tuesday shelled Hussein Aideed's south Mogadishu "presidential" palace and other positions held by his forces.
The round of violence erupted last Friday and has killed an estimated 135 people, according to Somali security sources.
But aid workers said they feared the true number of dead was much higher as fighters frequently did not publicise casualties as they feared the information would be useful to enemies.
"Some 900 people have been brought to hospitals with wounds since Friday so we would expect the death toll to be about one third of the wounded -- i.e. about 300," said an aid official.
The rival factions do not take dead to hospitals and bodies are often buried secretly by fellow fighters, aid workers said.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Tuesday 900 people had been were admitted to seven hospitals and medical centres in the city since Friday and more than 70 people had died of their wounds while undergoing medical treatment.

"We are appalled by the apparently high number of civilian casualties...a result of indiscriminate firing into places like markets where ordinary people gather," said Fred Grimm, head of ICRC Somalia.
"Thousands of people have left their homes to seek safety. Many of them have left Medina district in particular. If this continues public health problems could arise," Grimm added.
At least nine people were killed and 14 wounded in fighting on Tuesday night pitting Aideed's forces against militiamen loyal to Yalahow and his ally Hassan Ali Osman Atto, hospital sources said.
Four people including a woman were killed in a fuel storage depot by mortar explosions. Merchants moved their tankers away from the area on Wednesday and dozens of families fled.
Medina's population consists mostly of members of the same Abgal sub-clan as Ali Mahdi, the Aideed family's arch-enemy.
Before Ali Mahdi's faction entered the fray in earnest on Tuesday, street battles had centred on southern Mogadishu.
Fighting at Mogadishu airport with mortars and heavy weapons began when Aideed's forces thrust towards the southern end of the runway held by Yalahow's forces, allied with Ali Mahdi.

Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine, succeeded his father Mohamed Farah Aideed on his death in August and was elected president of Somalia by his own supporters. But both he and his government are rejected by most other faction leaders.
Mogadishu airport has been closed to all flights since the last U.N. peacekeepers pulled out of Somalia in March 1995.
